title: Kickoff notes — On‑prem offline artifact signing (signed offline bundles)
content:
Doc status: working notes (not a spec). Please add comments inline.

Meeting: Offline artifact signing kickoff (Redwood Private / air‑gapped installs)
Date/time: 2024-02-15 10:00–11:00 PT
Facilitator: Talia Benson
Note taker: Talia Benson (please correct if I missed anything)

Attendees
- Product: Vivek Kulkarni (Private Deployments), Naomi Feldman (Security & Compliance)
- Eng: Priya Natarajan (Platform sponsor), Ethan Park (installer/control plane), Connor O’Brien (Release Eng), Sahana Iyer (Build/CI), (Benji Okafor optional — couldn’t make it)
- Security: Marcus Lin (Sec Eng), Kevin Osei (audit/export + enterprise controls)
- SE/Field: Markus Klein, Fatima Noor
- Infra: Irene Choi (offline repo/media constraints)

Why we’re here (problem statement)
Regulated/air‑gapped customers require us to ship Redwood Private as an “offline bundle” (images + charts/manifests + binaries) moved via removable media or disconnected repo.
Today we have checksums in a few places, but there’s no cohesive integrity/provenance story and verification isn’t fail‑closed.
We need a v1 that: (1) works fully offline, (2) is auditable, (3) is operationally sane for releases and key management.

High-level goal (v1)
- Define offline bundle format (layout + manifest + digests) and sign it.
- Publish signed bundles through our artifact distribution path.
- Installer verifies signature + digests offline before unpack/install; fail‑closed default.
- Allow break-glass override only with explicit acknowledgement + audit trail.
- Provide internal runbooks + customer-facing verification/install guide.

Non-goals (explicitly agreed)
- Customer-managed signing (customer provides keys and signs Redwood artifacts) is NOT in v1.
- We are not trying to redesign all artifact distribution; only the offline/air‑gapped path.

Agenda
1) Customer requirements recap (SE)
2) Threat model framing (Security)
3) Proposed bundle/signing approach (Eng)
4) Installer verification UX + break-glass (Eng/Sec)
5) Ownership, timeline, and next steps

Customer requirements recap (Markus/Fatima)
- Must work with zero outbound network access at install time.
- Customers want a simple “verify” command they can run before install and during audits.
- Need clarity on key rotation: “If you rotate signing keys, will older bundles still verify?”
- In practice, customers move artifacts via: USB, internal artifact repo (Nexus/Artifactory), or staged VM that bridges networks (sneakernet).
- Common failure modes we’ve seen in air-gapped pilots:
  - Partial/corrupted transfers
  - Operators unpacking/repacking bundles incorrectly
  - Proxying images into local registry and losing exact digests/tags mapping

Threat model framing (Marcus)
- Main attacker: can tamper with offline bundle in transit or at rest (USB/drive/internal repo) OR can attempt rollback/downgrade.
- We are NOT assuming installer host is uncompromised in all cases, but we do want strong integrity checks to make tampering evident.
- Requirements:
  - Integrity + authenticity of bundle contents
  - Downgrade protection: ensure “verified” doesn’t mean “any old version” unless explicitly permitted
  - Audit-friendly logs for verification outcomes

Bundle format & signing approach (Connor/Sahana/Ethan) — early proposal
- Bundle includes:
  - OCI images (either as tarballs / OCI layout) + an images list
  - Helm charts or rendered manifests
  - Installer binaries + any helper tools
  - A single manifest file with:
    - schema version
    - release version
    - list of artifacts + per-artifact digests
    - build/provenance pointers (commit SHAs, build IDs)
- Sign at the “bundle-level” (sign the manifest / signing envelope) AND include per-artifact digests.
- Signature verification should not require internet.
- Key custody: KMS/HSM-backed signer service; no developer laptops.

Discussion notes / decisions (tentative)
1) Fail-closed verification in installer
- Decision: Default behavior is fail-closed. If verification fails, install halts prior to unpack/apply.
- Rationale: Air-gapped environments have higher risk and fewer compensating controls.
- Follow-up: define exact “preflight” stage so we can verify without side effects.

2) Break-glass override
- Decision: We will support an override for emergencies, but it must be explicit and auditable.
- Requirements brainstorm:
  - CLI flag + typed acknowledgement string (example: “I_ACKNOWLEDGE_VERIFICATION_FAILED”)
  - Log an audit event including bundle version, reason code, and operator-provided ticket/approval reference
  - Warn that support may ask for logs + may not proceed until integrity is established
- Open question: who is authorized to use override (customer role vs Redwood SE) and what approvals are required.

3) Downgrade/rollback protections
- Tentative: Manifest includes release version and a monotonically increasing build number; installer compares to current installed version.
- Open: what are the actual rules? (e.g., allow same major/minor, disallow older than currently installed unless a “--allow-downgrade” flag is set)

4) Determinism / reproducibility
- Connor raised: If manifests aren’t deterministic, we’ll get signature churn and poor debuggability.
- Action: include “manifest generation determinism” as an acceptance criterion (ordering, normalized fields, timestamps).

5) Artifact type coverage
- Requirement: One verification story across: images, charts, binaries, config bundles.
- Open: do we embed SBOM/provenance artifacts inside the bundle or provide offline references (files) that can be validated separately?

6) Publishing/distribution
- Infra note (Irene): Some customers require artifact storage paths that can be mirrored (simple directory layout). Avoid too many remote lookups.
- Action: propose a stable storage layout for bundles + detached signatures.

Initial requirements list (v1)
Functional
- “redwood-private-installer verify-bundle <path>” command (or equivalent) that:
  - validates signature using embedded trust root / bundled public cert(s)
  - checks manifest schema version is supported
  - verifies per-artifact digests against actual bytes on disk (or for images, against image tar/oci-layout digest)
  - outputs a machine-readable summary + human-readable status
- Installer install path calls verify step automatically before unpack/install.
- Verification works with network disabled.
- Break-glass flow requires explicit acknowledgement and records an audit entry.

Security
- Signing keys stored and used in KMS/HSM-backed workflow.
- Signed metadata ties back to:
  - release version
  - git commit SHAs for key repos (installer, helm charts, runtime tooling)
  - CI build ID
- Document key rotation and revocation story.

Observability / auditability
- Structured logs for: verification success/failure, failure reasons, override usage, bundle metadata.
- Exportable evidence artifacts for compliance: signature, manifest, verification logs.

Compatibility
- Bundle schema versioned; forward-compat behavior defined (e.g., installer errors clearly if schema > supported).
- Compatibility matrix for bundle ↔ installer versions (at least documented; ideally encoded).

Open questions (parked)
- What is our signing primitive?
  - Options mentioned: cosign (key pair), in-toto style attestations, TUF-like metadata.
  - Marcus: prefer something we can justify and maintain long-term; avoid bespoke crypto.
- Trust root distribution:
  - Do we ship the public key/cert with installer? How do we update it in air-gapped environments?
- Multiple signatures / multiple keys:
  - Do we need to support more than one active signing key at a time (for rotation)? Likely yes.
- Replay / downgrade:
  - What’s our formal policy for preventing replay of older signed bundles?
- Supportability:
  - What exact diagnostic bundle should customers send when verification fails?
- Image verification specifics:
  - If customer imports images into their local registry, what exactly are we verifying post-import?
  - Do we require customers to install from the bundle’s images directly, or allow mirroring while preserving digests?

Ownership (initial)
- Bundle format + manifest schema: Connor O’Brien (Release Eng) + Devon Price (release tooling) — with security review by Marcus Lin
- Signing pipeline/KMS integration: Sahana Iyer + Hanae Suzuki (as needed)
- Installer verification + CLI UX: Ethan Park + Benji Okafor
- Break-glass policy + wording: Naomi Feldman + Marcus Lin
- Audit logging + evidence mapping: Kevin Osei + Olga Petrov
- Customer workflow + pilot feedback loop: Markus Klein + Fatima Noor

Where work will live (tracking)
- PM initiative: Linear PM-482 — “Offline signed bundles for air-gapped installs”
- Engineering epics/issues (draft):
  - ENG-3912 — offline bundle format + manifest
  - ENG-3913 — add signing step to release pipeline
  - ENG-3914 — installer verify signature + digests (fail-closed)
  - ENG-3915 — break-glass override flow + audit logging
  - ENG-3916 — SBOM/provenance links in bundle

Early doc links (placeholders; we’ll replace with actual Confluence URLs once created)
- Confluence (to create): Offline bundles overview
- Confluence (to create): Offline bundle format spec v1
- Confluence (to create): Installer verification design
- Confluence (to create): Threat model — offline artifact signing
- Confluence (to create): ADR — offline bundle signing approach

Action items
1) (Talia) Create Linear project board and ensure above issues are linked to PM-482. Due: 2024-02-16
2) (Connor) Draft bundle directory layout + manifest field list (1-pager) and post in #eng thread. Due: 2024-02-20
3) (Sahana) Identify current release pipeline insertion point + estimate build time impact for signing stage. Due: 2024-02-22
4) (Ethan) Propose installer CLI UX + exit codes + where verification gates the install. Due: 2024-02-22
5) (Marcus/Naomi) Write initial threat model outline + break-glass policy requirements (what’s allowed / not allowed). Due: 2024-02-23
6) (Kevin) Define what audit events/log fields we need for SOC2-style evidence and customer audits. Due: 2024-02-23
7) (Markus/Fatima) Provide 2–3 customer “day in the life” flows (USB transfer vs internal repo mirroring) + must-have UX requirements. Due: 2024-02-21

Next meeting
- 2024-02-26: Review draft manifest schema + agree on signing approach and key custody plan.

Notes to self (Talia)
- Keep v1 tight: bundle signing + verify + docs + key ops. Don’t boil the ocean on SLSA/in-toto unless it materially helps regulated deals.
- Make sure we have crisp failure messages and a troubleshooting path; otherwise support will drown during pilots.
